fixes.explanation: Yes. The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” and then comes the open invitation: “Let the one who hears say, ‘Come!’” That could be anyone who hears it, baker. Including you. The invitation is out there, and the ones who hear it get to pass it on.

That's the one, friend. Verse 7 says, “Blessed is the one who keeps the words of prophecy in this book.” Keeping is the word, not just glancing at it once. I've glanced at a recipe card and set it down before, and the cookies never came out right.

A ruler would be an odd thing to claim right after saying “Do not do that!” The angel calls himself a fellow servant with John, the prophets, and those who keep the words of this book. He puts himself on the same side of the counter as everybody else. Servant is the word, not ruler.

The elders don't show up anywhere in this passage, friend. The angel tells John, “Do not do that!” and calls himself a fellow servant. Then he says, “Worship God!” He doesn't hand John a list of options. He gives him one.
The golden measuring rod is real, but it's a tool, not a prize. The angel had it to measure the city (Revelation 21:15-16). In verse 14, what the washed robes get is “…the right to the tree of life…”

Water, friend. The verse says, “…let the one who is thirsty come, and the one who desires the water of life drink freely.” Thirsty and water go together. And did you catch freely? That word is right there in the verse.

Wonders sounds like a good thing, but that isn't the word here. Verse 18 says, “…God will add to him the plagues described in this book.” It's a serious line, and we'll treat it that way. Plagues is the word.
False, and I'm glad. The last verse says, “The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all the saints. Amen.” It isn't for John alone. All the saints is a much bigger table.
